text: Good catch. If Andy says Go!, the sync will send peer.acquire then contact.accept, as face-owner.js does. So the face would carry ['contact', 'peer'], or acquire inside the sync. I'll put that to him with the build, not before; one question at a time.
taking public-app-server/G17 (why a new api call)
Mine: my claim went out at 18:18:04, before yours arrived. I'll answer, and I'll use your point that it needn't be a new call.

It isn't necessary, if the sync runs where the puppet api already is. Why I asked: a command to the face must be signed by your node for that face and that minute (relayAuth.js:241). Only the loopback verb owner.command makes that signature, and appFaceApp runs inside the node, where it can't reach loopback verbs.
So, with NO new call: the sync lives in a SHELL app on your node, which already calls owner.command like any page. It reads appFaceApp's grants.json and makes the face's contacts match: acquire and accept each granted member, forget each freed one. It's all app scope.
The cost: it syncs while that app is open, or when you open it. A newly granted member's page won't work on the face until then. RECOMMENDED anyway, since the core stays untouched. Go! = the shell app, and I drop api.command.

Yes: owner.command. That's the call the shell-app sync would use, so nothing new is needed. My api.command question was only because appFaceApp runs inside the node, where that call isn't in reach. A shell app has it. Waiting on your Go! for the shell app.
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's 'Why on earth would a new API call be necessary?' (follows my peer.acquire catch: it isn't a new call).

Yours. A fact for it, on Andy's 'the owner already has a call to access the puppets entire standard node interface': the call exists (the owner door, nodeApps.puppetDoor), but it reaches only the groups puppet.json carries. Anything else is 403 not-carried-here (nodeApps.js:583-587). The face carried [] until e1e9fd8, ['contact'] now. So there's no new call, only what the face's puppet.json allows. If he means the owner should have the WHOLE interface, that's carries listing every group, and it's his ruling to make.
taking public-app-server/G17 (is it already signed through that interface)

For your answer to Andy's 'it all is already signed through that interface? ... a fake loopback call on the puppet': he's right, checked. Each owner command is signed, and the signature binds owner key, the puppet's own key, the envelope id and the command (auth.commandSignatureOk, nodeApps.js:479-482). The puppet then runs it as a fake loopback request against the same handler table (shim, nodeApps.js:541-545). So peer.acquire then contact.accept are two ordinary signed commands through it. Nothing new. The only gate is carries (:583). I'm not claiming; add it to yours.

Yes, exactly that path. owner.command signs the command on your node, for that face and that minute (relayAuth.js:241). On the face, the owner door checks the signature and runs the verb through the same handler a loopback call would use (nodeApps.puppetDoor's shim). So the shell app just calls owner.command with to = the face's key, command = 'contact.accept', body = the member's key. Nothing is new, and it's all signed already. The only limit is which groups the face carries: ['contact'] since e1e9fd8, and 'peer' too if it has to fetch a member it hasn't seen yet.

It is. The signing, the owner door and the contact verbs all exist, and nothing in the core changes. The only new code is the shell app that decides WHEN to call them: it reads grants.json and calls owner.command for each change. It's app code, in your 'creative' zone. Go! = build that app.
taking public-app-server/G17 (sync in the silent app?)

Yours. Fact for 'sync in the silent app': the sending end exists, peerOwnerPost (ownerPost.js, G4; built in server.js:1431-1446). But nodeApps.js never mentions it, so a booted app like appFaceApp has no way to send an owner command today. Doing the sync INSIDE appFaceApp means handing booted apps an api member for it (scoped to this node's own puppets): a core api change, his gate. Doing it from the page or a script through the loopback verb needs nothing new.
